thread.title: Key Words: Tim Cook says his employees are not focused on Apple’s stock price

title: Key Words: Tim Cook says his employees are not focused on Apple’s stock price
text:
Published: Feb 21, 2018 2:15 p.m. ET Share 
Apple CEO says he previously worked at a company where everyone seemed to be monitoring share-price moves Getty Tim Cook at the Allen & Co. conference in Idaho in August 2016. 
By ‘I worked at a company a while back, many years ago, where every hallway you go in, you would see their stock price being monitored. You will not find that here.’ Tim Cook 
That’s Tim Cook, Apple’s CEO, painting a picture of a highly focused atmosphere at the company, during a wide-ranging interview with Fast Company . 
The reason, he hastens to add, is not solely that you can now get share-price updates on your iPhone instead. 
Cook’s résumé, for readers curious about which past employer he might have been drawing the contrast with, features stints of 12 years and six years, respectively, at IBM IBM, +0.40% and Compaq. 
For anyone more interested than the Cook-described Apple AAPL, +0.94% staff in the stock’s minute-to-minute performance, it’s currently up 1.1% at $173.75. So far in 2018, the stock is up 2.4%, as compared with the 2.1% rise of the Dow industrials DJIA, +0.60% . Apple is a Dow stock.
